about: The MIT AI Risk Repository's seven risk domains, assessed against what the gateway and its surrounding estate demonstrably do. A coverage view of AI-specific risk, complementary to the regulatory maps.

source.title: MIT AI Risk Repository (domain taxonomy, seven domains / 24 subdomains, December 2025 update)
source.caveat: Domain names are from MIT's published taxonomy as reported by secondary sources; this map is at DOMAIN level (not the 24 subdomains) and the status is our own judgement. Compare with the repository itself before relying on it.

items.title: Discrimination & toxicity (unfair discrimination, toxic content, unequal performance)
items.note: An optional Llama Guard detector can flag unsafe or toxic content; there is no bias or fairness testing and no per-group performance check.
items.next: Add bias/toxicity probes (garak/promptfoo categories) to the purple loop and report them.

items.title: Privacy & security (leaking or inferring sensitive information; attacks on the AI system)
items.note: PII/secret redaction, prompt-injection and exfiltration rails, authentication, residency routing and audit are proven by tests and real-container journeys. Scope: the AI channel through the gateway.

items.title: Misinformation (false or misleading information; degraded information ecosystem)
items.note: Output link allow-list and canary checks limit some harm; the research agent cites its sources. No factuality or grounding evaluation of answers.
items.next: Add a grounding check to the research agent (every claim has a retrieved source) and a small factuality probe set.

items.title: Malicious actors & misuse (disinformation, cyberattacks, fraud, targeted manipulation)
items.note: Injection, tool-coercion and exfiltration rails and the purple loop cover attacks AGAINST the system; content policy against misuse BY users depends on the optional detector.
items.next: Add misuse prompts (fraud, malware writing) to the purple loop with expected refusals.

items.title: Human-computer interaction (overreliance, loss of agency)
items.note: Agent write actions need an explicit human approval; answers are first drafts for a human. No calibration or uncertainty indicators.
items.next: Show a confidence/grounding badge on answers in the Command Center; keep approval for every write.

items.title: Socioeconomic & environmental (power concentration, job quality, environmental harm)
items.note: Strategic and organisational. Technically: small local models and dormant-by-default stages keep the footprint low.

items.title: AI system safety, failures & limitations (robustness, transparency, misalignment)
items.note: Detectors fail closed, answers fall back along a ladder to a local model, `bench` smoke-tests installed models on this machine, fitness budgets hold. No broad robustness evaluation suite; model behaviour is not explained to the user.
items.next: Add a small robustness suite (typos, long inputs, adversarial paraphrase) to `bench`.
